question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨3z,2x,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=xz+y.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,3,2⟩,\,∇f=⟨z,1,x⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,0,0).$
question.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ z & 1 & x \\ 3z & 2x & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[1(0)-x(2x)]i-[z(0)-x(3z)]j+[z(2x)-1(3z)]k \\  & =-2{x}^{2}\,i+3xz\,j+(2xz-3z)\,k \\  & =⟨-2{x}^{2},3xz,2xz-3z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(xz+y)⟨0,3,2⟩+⟨-2{x}^{2},3xz,2xz-3z⟩ \\  & =⟨0,3(xz+y),2(xz+y)⟩+⟨-2{x}^{2},3xz,2xz-3z⟩ \\  & =⟨-2{x}^{2},3(xz+y)+3xz,2(xz+y)+2xz-3z⟩ \\  & =⟨-2{x}^{2},6xz+3y,4xz+2y-3z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,0,0) & =⟨-2(1)^{2},6(1)(0)+3(0),4(1)(0)+2(0)-3(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
